course_description:
This course introduces students to the principles and practice of geotechnical design and implementation across the open pit mine lifecycle, covering geotechnical model development, slope design and optimisation, slope monitoring and instrumentation, slope stability management (including dewatering, rockfall, and large instabilities), and final pit closure. The course supports students’ development as mining professionals by building the geotechnical capability required to design, assess, and manage safe and effective slopes. Through seven structured online modules, students analyse real world geotechnical data, apply industry tools and frameworks (including slope design software), interpret monitoring information, and work through applied design and risk scenarios that mirror engineering practice in operational mining contexts.

The course consists of seven online modules, each focusing on key aspects of slope design and management, including foundational knowledge of geotechnical model construction, slope design and monitoring, geotechnical risk management, and slope closure. The seven modules covered are:

The Slope Design and Optimisation module will be further supported by the use of the RocScience software package. Details and access instructions will be provided at the start of the course. Students are also encouraged to make use of any slope design software tools available at their respective sites, if they wish.

course_aims: The course aims to equip students with technical expertise and practical skills needed for rock slope engineering. Students will learn to evaluate and apply integrated solutions for slope stability design and optimisation, groundwater management, rockfall mitigation, slope monitoring, and the closure of open pits and waste dumps, using industry tools and frameworks to support safe geotechnical practices across the open pit mine lifecycles.

learning_outcomes.description: Critically evaluate geological, structural, and geotechnical data collection techniques and interpret results to inform rock mass characterisation.
Develop and apply advanced geotechnical models and software tools to inform slope stability assessments and design decisions.
Design and optimize open pit slope and waste dump geometries by integrating geotechnical parameters, stability criteria, and economic constraints.
Assess and interpret data from advanced slope monitoring systems and instrumentation to detect instability indicators and inform proactive geotechnical decision-making.
Evaluate the impact of groundwater and surface water on slope stability and design effective dewatering systems.
Analyse mechanisms of rockfalls and structure dominant slope instabilities, apply predictive and mitigation techniques, and formulate remediation strategies.
Critically review existing geotechnical risk assessment frameworks used by Australian mining companies and develop risk management plans to address slope instability through case studies.
Design geotechnically stable open pit and water dump closure plans that meet regulatory standards.

assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This component involves pitching slope design and management project proposal via a PowerPoint presentation of no more than 10 minutes covering the following elements: Background: Provide a brief description of the operation you have selected and context on a selected task (e.g., is it a new slope, or an improvement to an existing slope?) Project objectives: Outline the main objectives of this project Project scope and methodology: Outline the scope (or tasks) of the design project and briefly describe the approach required to achieve the key objectives Project resources: Describe the required resources (e.g., data collection and software requirements etc) to conduct this project Project timeline: Propose the timeline for each of the project objectives Project risks: Briefly identify the risks to completing this project within the required timeframe and any mitigation strategies that can be put in place Please refer to Blackboard for detailed marking criteria. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. assessment_details.title: Progress Brief
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This component involves the review and selection of a new slope design and implementation, improvement, or failure remediation at your operation. If you are not in an operational setting, a real case study will be made available. You will be required to submit a two-page project brief using the available fillable PDF template. The project brief provides basic information about the design evaluation and improvement project that you will be conducting and includes the following: Background: Provide a brief description of the operation, mining method and current slope design and management activities Problem statement: Provide context on a selected design and specific slope stability concerns that would benefit from a revision and/or evaluation. Consultation with your colleagues and supervisors is expected. Project objectives: Outline the main objectives of this design evaluation and improvement project. Value proposition: Outline the potential benefits of this design evaluation project. Project methodology: Outline the scope of the design evaluation and briefly describe the approach required to achieve the key objectives. Required resources: List all resources required for the successful execution of the project, together with their availability status and, where applicable, the strategy for obtaining them Project plan and risks: Briefly provide a delivery plan against key objectives and identify the risks to completing this project. Please refer to Blackboard for a detailed marking criteria. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance.
